passages.provision_quote: Following the implementation of the minimum wage increase specified in subparagraph (F) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), on or before August 1 of that year, and on or before each August 1 thereafter, the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage. The calculation shall increase the minimum wage by the lesser of 3.5 percent and the rate of change in the averages of the most recent July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period over the preceding July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period for the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics nonseasonally adjusted United States Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (U.S. CPI-W). The result shall be rounded to the nearest ten cents ($0.10). Each adjusted minimum wage increase calculated under this subdivision shall take effect on the following January 1.
passages.note: Chaptered text; SEC. 3 amends Labor Code 1182.12 to step the floor up to fifteen dollars ($15) per hour and then index it annually to the U.S. CPI-W, and the bill's other part (paid sick days for in-home supportive services providers) is keyed to those same wage levels rather than being an unrelated subject.

rows.reasoning: Allen voted Aye on Senate concurrence in SB 3 (2015-2016), whose operative section raises the state wage floor on a schedule to fifteen dollars ($15) per hour and then directs that "the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage" each year by the U.S. CPI-W, taking effect "on the following January 1" with no further legislation. That matches both clauses of the rung that would "Raise the wage floor and tie it to the cost of living, so it rises automatically each year without new legislation", and the standing indexation excludes the rung that would "Raise the wage floor to a set higher level, then adjust it only when lawmakers vote to."
